subject: Private/VPC design: ownership matrix + evidence asks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita.rao@medicore.com>, Medicore Security Team <security@medicore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private/VPC design: ownership matrix + evidence asks

Hi Anita / Medicore security team —

Thanks again for the call earlier. This thread is a short recap and the concrete asks we discussed so your reviewers have what they need. High-level: Medicore is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) to host inference in a customer-managed VPC with optional air-gapped nodes for regulatory workloads.

What we covered and immediate next steps we promised:
- Ownership: you asked for a clear matrix showing which networking components Medicore manages vs Redwood (routing/NAT, VPN, bastion, private endpoints, peering). I'm attaching a draft VPC diagram that maps responsibilities; please flag anything we misunderstood.
- Evidence: you requested SOC 2 status, recent penetration test summary, and a minimal list of artifacts we can surface quickly (audit logs retention, KMS integration notes). We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted pentest summary under NDA.
- Data flow: we sketched the inference data path (client -> VPC ingress -> private inference cluster -> S3-backed model artifact storage). You wanted to confirm that model artifacts and KV cache never egress to public internet unless explicitly configured.
- Air-gap: discussed two options — fully air-gapped on-prem nodes with manual model sync, or a hybrid where sensitive models run on dedicated offline nodes. You asked for constraints and the operational lift for each option.

Attached: redwood_vpc_draft_diagram.png (ownership overlay), vendor_questionnaire_template.xlsx (our questionnaire to jumpstart your security team), medicore_hosting_constraints.pdf (notes from product about air-gap limitations).

Concrete asks for Medicore security team (please reply inline):
1) Confirm ownership corrections on the attached diagram by EOD Tue 20 Mar.
2) Which artifacts are immediately required to proceed with procurement (SOC 2 + pentest + encryption spec)?
3) Indicate whether HIPAA or additional regional data residency constraints apply to the datasets you plan to route through Redwood Private.

I'll loop in Karthik to follow up on the technical answers once you share the diagram comments. Happy to jump on a short follow-up with your infra/security SMEs next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few quick notes from our side after review this morning:
- The diagram looks right in general; we'll add our managed VPN concentrator and a note that our SOC 2-scoped S3 buckets are on our account. Expect the annotated diagram by Tue.
- For procurement we need: SOC 2 Type II (most recent), encryption-at-rest spec (KMS provider + key rotation), and a summary of network hardening controls (firewall rules + bastion process). The pentest summary will be optional for first approval but required before production sign-off.
- Medicore will need an explicit statement about whether model KV cache can be configured to keep data entirely inside the VPC (no external caching). Please have your infra team confirm.

HIPAA applies for a subset of workloads (PHI-containing inference). We will separate the proof points for HIPAA-scoped workloads vs non-PHI experiments.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with the primary reviewers and their timelines; security@medicore will be the central intake.

Best,

Hi Anita / team —

Quick technical clarifications from our side to help your reviewers evaluate feasibility: 
1) KV cache: Our runtime supports an in-VPC KV cache backed by ephemeral instance storage or an EBS volume instantiated inside your VPC. There is no mandatory external caching; egress only occurs if you enable cross-region replication or an external cache. We will document the configuration you need to ensure zero egress.
2) KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault). Key rotation policies are configurable and audited; we'll provide the KMS integration guide and an example IAM policy.
3) Network hardening: we enforce least-privilege SGs at the instance level and recommend a dedicated management bastion with MFA and short TTL session tokens. We'll provide a one-page checklist for your ops team.

I'll attach a short tech appendix and a checklist; Vanessa, Marissa — can you confirm which artifacts we'll surface immediately (SOC 2 PDF and a redacted pentest summary under NDA)? Marissa, I know you have the latest SOC export.

-Karthik
